name: Rummy
description: Rummy is a classic draw-and-discard matching game. Players form melds (sets of three or four of a kind, or runs of three or more in suit) and try to dispose of all cards. Draw one, meld and lay off optionally, discard one. First to go out wins; others count deadwood points.

content.text: Rummy is a classic draw-and-discard matching game. Players form melds (sets of three or four of a kind, or runs of three or more in suit) and try to dispose of all cards. Draw one, meld and lay off optionally, discard one. First to go out wins; others count deadwood points.

Rummy games first appeared in the early twentieth century. Two main theories: Mexican origin from Conquian (first attested 1852), or Asian from a Mahjong-related game such as Kun P'ai. The draw-and-discard principle with melding appears in Chinese card games from the 18thâ€“19th century. The name 'rummy' may derive from British slang ('rum' = odd), Rum Poker, or the drink.

items.text: Going Rummy: If you go out in one turn without having melded or laid off before, score is doubled (or +10 bonus).
No Lay-Off Until Meld: You may not lay off on others' melds until you have melded at least once.
Ace High or Low: Aces can be high (Q-K-A) or low (A-2-3). Aces then count 15 in deadwood.
Block Rummy: Discard pile is not reused. When stock runs out and next player doesn't want the discard, game ends. Lowest deadwood wins.
500 Rummy: Multiple cards can be taken from discard; points for melds; play to 500.
